title: New feature: Import settings from file system
body:
It might be easy to keep it in 1 folder and 1 file to export/import.
But sadly not everyone has "SD" to save to or load from.
And I can't seem to find a good way to restore the settings.
If I click export settings, it goes to the "download" folder.
But if I try and import, it does not work, the image below will show that having the new config file in downloads does not let it get imported.
So maybe let us find the file and click import instead of an auto check for 1 location?
(The app has all permissions the phone can give, OnePlus 8 Pro EU, android 11)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4199669/106401182-0aa2b380-6423-11eb-9fd8-5f1a5e3b48f0.png)

comments.body: This is similar to the following and would address both things. https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/issues/1622

Why do you think it doesn't work?

I just tested this on Jan.29, 2021.  But, I don't think there is anything new about it.  It worked with much older versions as well.

I emptied the Downloads folder.
Under Import/Export features, tapped on Load/Save Settings on SD card.

Tapped on LOAD all settings from SDCARD.  Got the message could not load preferences.

Then, tapped on Save all settings to SD card.  It saved xDrip-export in the Downloads folder.
Changed the Hardware data source from disabled (test phone) to Nightscout follower.
Went back to Load/Save Settings on SD card and tapped on Load all settings from SDcard. 
It worked.  The data source was back to disabled.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4199669/107677337-6fb79e00-6c9a-11eb-9e5b-62ac8e151730.png)

There is always room for improvement.
If you look at the pull requests, you will see that it takes a very long time for a change to be approved.  One of the reasons is that a fix should not cause any new malfunctions even for older devices.  And it takes time and effort to verify that.

I don't think anyone disagrees that what you are suggesting is an improvement.

My only point is that you should be able to import settings as is with the existing code.  

The other issue you have linked to is exactly the same in that sense.  After you export settings, you can easily rename the file, may be give it a date suffix.  Again, it is an improvement.  But, you can accomplish the objective with the code as is.

Put those in contrast with a scenario where a parent cannot follow her child's readings because a new version of Android has broken the xDrip code.  
Therefore, she cannot send the kid to school.  
If I have a say, I would prioritize the latter case.
